scope: Focused review and revision of proposal 07 after the initial soft-pd-cache-scheduling-2026-11-17 synthesis. Adds primary-source papers for holder/executor scheduling, closed-loop stability, load-versus-recompute decisions and cache discovery; updates PPD and DualPath publication identities; revises the path, memory and evaluation model. This record describes a research design and archived mechanisms. It does not report a prototype, framework capability audit, novelty proof or GPU experiment.

artifacts.title: Evolving Infra: Agent-Adaptive LLM Serving at Scale
Vesta: Queueing-Aware LLM Scheduling for Real-World Workloads
Bursts That Outlast Themselves: Persistent Degradation in Prefix-Cached Agent Serving
When the KV Cache Is Slower Than the GPU: Scaling Remote KV Tiers for Context-Parallel Prefill
KVCompass: A Discovery Plane for Internet-Scale Prefix Cache Sharing in LLM Serving

mechanism_readings.finding: Vesta assigns each session a stable authoritative KV holder and independently selects an executor. A remote executor fetches the prefix and writes the new suffix back to the holder. Executor selection includes backlog, transfer work and a congestion price for additional service demand.

Evolving Infra combines shared node host-memory KV, peer reads, dynamic PD roles and branch/version reference counts. It is a direct baseline for shared L2, cache lifetime and effective role-capacity adaptation.

A remote hit can cost more than recomputation, and synchronous loading can overload an engine queue even with low GPU utilization. The paper models bandwidth plus fixed hit cost, shards and asynchronously loads the remote tier, and identifies load-or-recompute decisions as a next step.

Closed-loop agent sessions can sustain a degraded cache/recompute/backlog regime after a short trigger. Suspending admitted sessions and bounding active resident-KV demand recover the evaluated single-colocated-engine setting. Proposal 07 uses this budget as a common experimental constraint and separates path selection from admission control.

KVCompass decouples prefix identity from dynamic holder placement. False or stale locators affect forwarding performance while the selected worker validates usable local KV and recomputes missing tokens. Decode output enters its discovery index after a later prefill rather than through a decode-time publication protocol.

design_revisions: The primary question is joint warm-request path selection under fixed GPU count and fixed session decode binding. Sustained-load adaptation is an evaluation scenario for effective warm-prefill capacity.
R is an explicit full/partial recompute path alongside A/B/C/D. Every cached path is compared with recompute under the same transfer and memory model.
Cache tier and holder are orthogonal state. L2 includes local and peer host-memory copies, and a source descriptor carries prefix, version, holder, tier and valid length.

Committed, loading, backing-up and evictable states enter the scheduler. Only published and validated contiguous prefixes form executable hits; directory hints share common validation and fallback rules.
Every path reserves and accounts for HBM history and incremental KV, append workspace, L2 staging, duplicate copies and HBM/DRAM byte-seconds.
B/C/D early decode binding and reservation time enter path cost. Dynamic decode binding is a separate experiment.
Vesta-style queueing externality is a required baseline and scheduler feature. Strata delay-hit merging is common across compared policies.
Closed-loop experiments use a common session working-set budget. Fixed-admission/path-only and fixed-path/admission-only ablations separate path gains from stability gains.
Append, rewrite and compaction requests use exact valid-prefix semantics. Position-independent and approximate cross-version reuse are extensions.
D-side append capacity directly offloads eligible warm work and indirectly frees P capacity for cold requests. Full physical role conversion remains in proposal 03.

Phase zero audits D-local append, D-to-P lazy reads, P/D storage reads, incremental return, peer L2 reads and publication/release events on the target framework before global scheduler implementation.
Evaluation compares against the strongest comparable composition of DualPath, PPD/AMPD and Vesta-style mechanisms, not only isolated single-mechanism baselines.
